differences: The clearer mask, warmer coat, and slimmer body are closer to the reference. However, the side muzzle still forms a long shallow shelf, and the lower face tapers to a central point beneath the mask rather than two soft cheek volumes around a compact nose.

The mask still determines most of the facial silhouette: a broad eye panel funnels into a long narrow nose pocket. The eyes retain a fixed round stare, so the face lacks the reference's relaxed, expressive cheek-and-eye relationship.

Fur geometry has regressed into conspicuous raised ridges, torn-looking tabs, and sharp isolated silhouette points. In side swim and bank views these read as damaged surface detail rather than soft fur.

Swim frames now show a real phase change through the abdomen and pelvis; the torso is no longer an unchanged capsule. Bank frames also show more body participation, and the dive now progresses from head anticipation into a whole-body descent.

The dive provides the strongest evidence of improved flow: frames 1–2 lead with the head, frames 3–5 involve the trunk and hips, and later frames bring the tail along. Its final frames crop the face and snorkel, preventing complete pose/intersection evaluation.
Tail and fin tips remain rather rigid wedge-like shapes even as their bases move. Their delayed orientation is improved, but the silhouettes could soften during stroke reversal.

The reference-match threshold is still not met by facial construction and fur finish. Real-time cadence, blend transitions, the revised beaver, and gameplay-distance appearance remain unverified in this round.
suggestions: P1 face: build a compact muzzle as an explicit sculpted volume integrated into the head rather than continuing to inflate the lower half of a sphere. Use subtle paired cheek fullness around the nose, a short rounded front, and an underside that returns quickly toward the neck; eliminate the horizontal jaw shelf.

P1 face: shorten the mask's nose pocket so it follows the compact muzzle instead of making a long downward point. Add a restrained upper eyelid contour and shorten the smile line, letting cheek volume carry the expression.

P1 fur: remove the raised mid-body tabs and jagged isolated points. Start with two or three broad, shallow, rearward-flowing clumps integrated into cheek/hip silhouette edges; keep their roots flush and their tips rounded. Restore additional fur only when the plain silhouette remains clean.

P2 motion: preserve the new head-to-trunk-to-pelvis dive timing and the traveling swim deformation. Refine tail/fin-tip bending at direction reversals instead of increasing whole-body amplitude further.

P2 verification: pull the dive camera back enough to retain the complete character for every frame, then provide a short real-time sequence to assess cadence and transitions. Apply the successful geometry decisions to the beaver and review both together before declaring a pass.
reasoning: The body animation has made a substantial qualitative advance and now demonstrates whole-body follow-through in the sampled poses. Facial anatomy and the conspicuous fur artifacts remain major reference mismatches, so the result still requires revision despite that motion improvement.
